Subject Re Detention of Russians by the S.C.G.Police

Made by S.I. Lunnings Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
 At 6.05 p.m. 18-11-39 a telephone message was received from the Officer i/c "D" Sector, "O" Post reporting that a foreigner with his wife and daughter had been detained by the S.C.G.Police at Great Western Railway crossing. Mr. Samson, Assistant Commissioner, together with S.I. Lunnings, D.S. Matsushita and C.D.S.219 attended.

 From enquiries made it was ascertained that the foreigner concerned i.e. Mr. and Mrs. B.L. Cooper and their daughter Mrs. V. Aumann (all Russians) had entered premises situated at No.211 Hungjao Road on permission from the Chinese caretaker, when a foreigner whom Mr. B.L. Cooper recognized as Mr. Fromm (German) entered the premises and order them to leave.

 Mr. Fromm objected to Mrs. Aumann gathering flowers of which she had a small bunch in her hand. Mr. B.L. Cooper left the premises and drove his motor car No.7309 towards the Settlement, when on arrival at Great Western Railway Crossing they were stopped by Mr. Fromm; who reported in Chinese to the S.C.G.Police that Mr. Cooper had stolen flowers from a garden at 211 Hungjao Road. Mr. & Mrs. B.L. Cooper and Mrs. Aumann were being questioned by a Chinese Interpreter, when a British Military Officer came to the railway crossing and called them across to the Settlement side of the perimeter which they did without interference by the S.C.G.Police or Japanese Military. Mr. B.L. Cooper left his M/Car on the Hungjao Side of the perimeter.

 Mr. Samson, A/Commissioner, together with D.S. Matsushita and C.D.S.219 interviewed the Japanese Military

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Mr. B.L. Cooper
native of Russia taken by S.I. Munnings
at 7 p.m. on the 18-11-39 and interpreted by

At about 4.45 p.m. 18-11-39 I accompanied by my wife,
and daughter, Mrs. V. Aumann visited premises situated at No.
211 Hungjao Road, where I have been given permission by the
Chinese caretaker to take a walk in the garden, and gather
flowers. At about 5.15 p.m. even date, whilst taking a walk
in the garden, I was approached by a foreigner whom I recogni-
zed as a Mr. Fromm, (German) he asked me what I was doing there
and who had given me permission to enter the premises. I
replied that I had been given permission by the Chinese care-
taker, and that I had visited this place on several occasions.
Mr. Fromm then asked my daughter (Mrs. Aumann) who had given
her permission to gather flowers, of which she had a small
bunch in her hand, Mrs. Aumann replied that she had been
given permission by the caretaker.

Mr. Fromm then ordered us to leave the premises, which
we complied with. I then drove my L/Car 7309 towards the
Settlement, when on arrival at the railroad crossing on Gt.
Western Road, I observed Mr. Fromm standing on the road near
the Japanese Military post, he signalled me to stop, which I
did. He then reported (in Chinese) to the S.C.G. Police to
the effect that I had been stealing flowers. We then alighted
from the car and were questioned by a Chinese interpreter
who explained the case to the Japanese Gendarmie; the Chinese
interpreter explained to Mr. Fromm that it was a very trivial
affair, but Mr. Fromm insisted that we be taken to the S.C.G.
P.B. Headquarters.

It appeared that the Interpreter suggested we reported to

1939年11月18日下午约4时45分，我陪同妻子
和女儿 V. Aumann 夫人，访问了位于
虹桥路211号的场所，中国看守人已允许我在花园里散步并采集
花朵。同日约下午5时15分，当我在花园里散步时，
一名被我认出是 Fromm 先生（德国人）的外国人走近我，他问我在那里做什么，
以及谁允许我进入该场所。我
回答说，是中国看守人允许的，而且我曾多次
访问过这个地方。
随后 Fromm 先生询问我的女儿（Aumann 夫人），是谁允许她采集花朵的，当时她手中握着一小束花。Aumann 夫人回答说，是看守人允许的。

随后 Fromm 先生命令我们离开该场所，我们
照办了。随后我驾驶我的 L/Car（轻型汽车）7309 号驶向
租界，当到达大西路（Gt. Western Road）的铁路道口时，
我看到 Fromm 先生站在靠近日本军方岗哨的路边，他示意我停车，我
便停了车。随后他用中文向中国市政府警察（S.C.G. Police）报告，
大意是我在偷花。随后我们下车，由一名中文翻译
向日本宪兵队解释案情；该中文翻译向 Fromm 先生解释说，这是一件非常琐碎的
小事，但 Fromm 先生坚持要将我们带往中国市政府警察
总局。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. ________
Narcotic Section Station,
STRICTLY CONFIDENTIAL REPORT
Date March 23, 1933.
Subject (in full) Ervin Rybar Fromm
Made by D.I. Papp Forwarded by Supt. Quayle

Referring to file D.4646, I respectfully beg to
forward the following information regarding E. Rybar Fromm :-
According to information E. Rybar Fromm is stated to
work for a very wealthy and influential Chinese named Ma Ziang
Sung (馬祥生) who is residing at 22 Route Pottier, French Con-
cession. Ma, it is stated, has amassed his fortune by
trafficking in morphine and Hwo Wei Lottery gambling in the
French Concession and is reported to be engaged of late in the
smuggling of curios to U.S.A. This is significant in view of
the fact that E. Rybar Fromm is frequently visiting ships,
arriving from and departing to U.S.A.
Ma Ziang Sung (馬祥生) is reported to have considerable
influence in governmental circles and is stated to be a good
friend of the former Minister of Foreign Affairs, Mr. C.T. Wang.

E. Papp
D.I.

Kneely under Route)
D.C. (Crime)

参照档案 D.4646，谨呈报有关 E. Rybar Fromm 的下列信息：-
据信，E. Rybar Fromm 为一名名为 Ma Ziang Sung（馬祥生）的富有且极具影响力的中国人工作，马居住于法租界蒲石路22号。据说，马通过在法租界贩卖吗啡和经营“华威”彩票赌博积累了财富，并据报道近期从事向美国走私古董的活动。鉴于 E. Rybar Fromm 频繁登上来往美国的船只，这一情况值得注意。
据报道，Ma Ziang Sung（馬祥生）在政府圈子里拥有相当大的影响力，并据称是前外交部长王正廷（C.T. Wang）先生的好友。

CONFIDENTIAL

S. B. REGISTRY
File No. D # 548
Section 2, S.B. / 133
REPORT
Date March 10, 1933.
Subject (in full) Enquiries in connection with Ervin Rybar Fromm, Manager of
the Mutual Insurance Co., 25 Jinkee Road.
Made by D.S. Tilton Forwarded by [Signature]

Ervin Rybar Fromm, Czecho Slovak, manager of the Mutual
Insurance Co., 25 Jinkee Road, residing at No. 303 Rue Bourgeat,
French Concession, the son of Joseph and Anna Rybar, former
Austrian subjects, was born in Prague on May 1, 1892.
Joseph Rybar, the father, is stated to have been an
officer in the Austrian Army, and to have committed suicide by
shooting himself when his son Rybar was quite young. The
widow then left her small son with some relatives, and went to
the U.S.A. where she met and married a Norwegian engineer named
C. A. Fromm. During 1908, the couple arrived in Shanghai
from the U.S.A. Sometime later the son, who was still of
school going age, also arrived in Shanghai and joined his
mother and step-father. The latter is at present employed
with the New Engineering and Shipbuilding Works Ltd., 640
Yangtzepoo Road, and registered at the local Norwegian Consulate.
During his early youth, Ervin Rybar Fromm, as he was then
known, obtained positions with German insurance firms including
Bornemann & Co., 8-B Peking Road, and Sander Wiesler & Co.,
8-B Peking Road, and is reputed to have shown great promise
and subsequently held positions of trust in the aforementioned
concerns. He continued in this employment until the outbreak
of the Great War when he lost his position in the latter
mentioned firm when it closed down.
In 1914 Fromm is reported to have received instructions
to return to Austria to join the army, and he left Shanghai
for Austria via the U.S.A. He arrived in San Francisco
where he is reported to have received orders from the Austrian
authorities to either remain there or return to Shanghai as
it was impossible for him to secure a passage to Austria.

日期 1933年3月10日。
主题（全称） 关于 Mutual Insurance Co.（互助保险公司，地址金介路25号）经理 Ervin Rybar Fromm 的调查。
制作人 侦探警佐 Tilton 转呈人 [签名]

Ervin Rybar Fromm，捷克斯洛伐克人，互助保险公司经理，公司地址金介路25号，居住于法租界布尔热瓦路303号，系 Joseph 和 Anna Rybar 之子，其父母原为奥地利臣民，于1892年5月1日出生于布拉格。
据称，其父 Joseph Rybar 曾是奥地利军队的一名军官，在儿子 Rybar 年幼时开枪自杀。遗孀随后将幼子托付给一些亲戚，自己前往美国，在那里结识并嫁给了一位名叫 C. A. Fromm 的挪威工程师。1908年间，这对夫妇从美国抵达上海。不久后，当时仍处于学龄的儿子也抵达上海，与母亲和继父团聚。继父目前受雇于杨树浦路640号的新工程造船有限公司（New Engineering and Shipbuilding Works Ltd.），并在当地挪威领事馆注册。
Ervin Rybar Fromm 早年（当时以此名闻名）曾在多家德国保险公司任职，包括北京路8-B号的 Bornemann & Co. 和北京路8-B号的 Sander Wiesler & Co.，据称表现出极大的前途，随后在上述公司担任受信任的职位。他一直在此任职，直到大战爆发，后者公司倒闭，他因此失去了在该公司的职位。
据报道，1914年 Fromm 接到指令返回奥地利参军，他经美国离开上海前往奥地利。他抵达旧金山，据称在那里接到奥地利当局的命令，要么留在那里，要么返回上海，因为他无法获得前往奥地利的船票。

As he was not holding any rank in the Austrian Army, and was
stated to be only a recruit, who had passed his preliminary
examination before the Austrian Consul in Shanghai, he decided
to return to Shanghai which he did immediately afterwards.

Apparently on his return to Shanghai he was unable to find
permanent employment as local German firms had been compelled
to suspend business. In 1915 Fromm first came under the
notice of the Municipal Police in consequence of his being
connected with the activities of a German named Adolph Neilsen,
a notorious spy, gun runner, arms and drug dealer, who came
into prominence in Shanghai during the Great War.

Fromm first became acquainted with Neilsen during their
business careers, and following the outbreak of the Great War,
it could be expected that the Austrians and Germans in Shanghai
would naturally bind themselves together in aid of the common
cause.

Fromm was not involved to any great extent in the arms
smuggling operations engineered by Neilsen and reported to be
directed from the German Consulate at that time, as may be gained
from a perusal of our records. It was then considered that
Fromm was not of sufficient importance to be kept under
surveillance by the Municipal Police as other members of the
Neilsen clique, and it is believed that Fromm was only a tool
in the hands of Neilsen.

Fromm evidently either experienced some distaste in
working with Neilsen or was of the opinion later that he was
being duped, for on November 16, 1916, he furnished information
to the Municipal Police of a case of arms smuggling by Neilsen.
Fromm is known to have stated that his actions in assisting

由于他在奥地利军队中没有任何军衔，且据称仅是一名新兵，曾在上海奥地利领事馆通过初步考试，他决定返回上海，并随即付诸实施。

显然，回到上海后，他无法找到固定工作，因为当地的德国公司被迫停业。1915年，弗罗姆（Fromm）首次引起工部局警务处的注意，原因是他与一名叫阿道夫·尼尔森（Adolph Neilsen）的德国人的活动有关联。尼尔森是一名臭名昭著的间谍、军火走私贩、武器和毒品商人，在大战期间于上海崭露头角。

弗罗姆是在职业生涯中初次结识尼尔森的，随着大战爆发，可以预料在上海的奥地利人和德国人自然会团结起来，以支持共同的事业。

从查阅我们的记录可知，弗罗姆并未深度参与由尼尔森策划、当时据报由德国领事馆指挥的军火走私行动。当时认为，弗罗姆不像尼尔森团伙的其他成员那样重要到需要被工部局警务处监视，据信弗罗姆仅仅是尼尔森手中的一枚棋子。

弗罗姆显然要么对与尼尔森共事感到厌恶，要么后来认为自己被欺骗了，因为他在1916年11月16日向工部局警务处提供了关于尼尔森军火走私案的情报。众所周知，弗罗姆曾声明，他协助

the Neilsen clique was purely from a political motive, and
at no time did he assist Neilsen for personal gain alone,
and was certainly not involved in the shady work such as
smuggling of drugs and dealing in opium as practiced by
Neilsen. However, it is significant to note that Fromm
and Neilsen were both implicated in a statement made to the
Municipal Police by a male Chinese who was arrested in possession
of a quantity of opium in September, 1916, as being the two
persons who had employed him to deliver the drug.
Fromm and Neilsen were later known to have been associated
together during 1917. In the following year Fromm apparently
proceeded to Austria.
In 1920 he returned to Shanghai in possession of a
Czecho-Slovak passport (he having been born in territory acceded
to Czecho-Slovak) and registered at the local Czecho-Slovak
Consulate.
Following his return to Shanghai, Fromm is stated to
have been connected with the former Yangtsze Trading Co.,
35 Jinkee Road, Insurance Department. During 1921 to 1925
he acted as the local agent for the Russian Insurance Company
of Copenhagen, with an office at 35 Jinkee Road.
During 1923 Fromm married a Russian widow named
Mikulovna Danilchuk nee Georgieff, born on April 17, 1892, at
Odessa. This marriage was not a success and resulted later
in a separation.
During 1925 he was connected with the Domino, and
Oriental Enterprise Co., an American concern with offices at
31 Jinkee Road. This firm later closed down after which
Fromm took up a position with Haskins and Sells, auditors,

尼尔森团伙 purely 是出于政治动机，他从未单纯为了个人利益而协助尼尔森，也肯定没有参与尼尔森所从事的诸如毒品走私和鸦片交易等不法勾当。然而，值得注意的是，弗罗姆和尼尔森均被卷入了一起案件：1916年9月，一名持有大量鸦片的华籍男子被捕，他在向工部局警务处所作的供词中指认这两人是雇佣他运送毒品的雇主。
后来已知弗罗姆和尼尔森在1917年间仍有往来。次年，弗罗姆显然前往了奥地利。
1920年，他持捷克斯洛伐克护照返回上海（他出生于划归捷克斯洛伐克的领土），并在当地捷克斯洛伐克领事馆注册。
据称，回到上海后，弗罗姆与前长江贸易公司（Yangtsze Trading Co.，江西路35号保险部）有关联。1921年至1925年间，他担任哥本哈根俄罗斯保险公司（Russian Insurance Company of Copenhagen）的本地代理，办公地点位于江西路35号。
1923年，弗罗姆娶了一位名叫米库洛夫娜·丹尼尔丘克（Mikulovna Danilchuk，娘家姓乔治耶夫 Georgieff）的俄罗斯寡妇为妻，她于1892年4月17日出生于敖德萨。这段婚姻并不成功，最终导致分居。
1925年，他与多米诺东方企业公司（Domino, and Oriental Enterprise Co.）有关联，这是一家美国公司，办公地点位于江西路31号。该公司后来倒闭，此后弗罗姆在会计师事务所哈斯金斯与塞尔斯（Haskins and Sells）任职，

6 Kiukiang Road, which he left in January, 1926, to take up the
local agency for the Taiheyo Insurance Co., head office Osaka.
In 1928, in company with A. G. Hearne, British, Fromm
established the Manufacturers Life Insurance Company at 25
Jinkee Road. A. G. Hearne died during 1932, and Fromm has
carried on the business from that time under the name of the
Mutual Insurance Co. at present acting as insurance brokers only.
Information has been gained that recently Dr. Fischer,
the prominent local lawyer, a friend of Fromm's, approached the
latter with a view to establishing him as an agent for The
Black Sea and Baltic General Insurance Co. Ltd., Head Office,
London, General Agency for China, No. 3 Foochow Road, and in
connection with the enterprise Dr. Fischer is stated to have
also introduced Fromm to The Far Eastern Bank (Dalbank) in order
to obtain the necessary bank references. The Far Eastern
Bank is stated to conduct banking business for the latter
mentioned insurance company.
Fromm is apparently anxious to secure this agency as at
present his business is not flourishing, and his future success
depends mainly on his obtaining some insurance agency which will
enable him to extend his connections.
He is also known to have confidentially stated that
rather than be involved with any Soviet enterprise in connection
with the above agency which may bring him into disfavour with
the Czecho-Slovak Consulate, he will abandon the projected move.
Apart from stating that Fromm is a reliable business man,
the local Czecho-Slovak Consulate know nothing about him.
Fromm is not widely known within Shanghai circles, and
he is regarded as a fairly reliable but not very successful

1928年，弗罗姆与英国人A. G. 赫恩（A. G. Hearne）合作，在江西路25号成立了制造商人寿保险公司（Manufacturers Life Insurance Company）。A. G. 赫恩于1932年去世，此后弗罗姆以互助保险公司（Mutual Insurance Co.）的名义继续经营业务，目前仅作为保险经纪人行事。
据悉，最近当地著名律师、弗罗姆的朋友费舍尔博士（Dr. Fischer）接触后者，旨在委任他为黑海与波罗的海综合保险公司有限公司（The Black Sea and Baltic General Insurance Co. Ltd.，总部伦敦，中国总代理处位于福州路3号）的代理。据称，为了获得必要的银行资信证明，费舍尔博士还就此项目将弗罗姆介绍给了远东银行（Dalbank）。据称，远东银行为上述保险公司办理银行业务。
弗罗姆显然急于获得这一代理权，因为他目前的生意并不景气，他未来的成功主要取决于能否获得某个保险代理权，从而扩展他的人脉关系。
另据悉，他曾私下表示，如果上述代理权涉及任何可能使他不受捷克斯洛伐克领事馆待见的苏维埃企业，他将放弃这一计划。
除了称弗罗姆是一位可靠的商人外，当地捷克斯洛伐克领事馆对他一无所知。
弗罗姆在上海圈子里知名度不高，他被认为是一位相当可靠但不太成功的
